en: Several pieces in Zhang’s
present explorations of a rapidly changing social environment amplified by the history of the exhibition site, its embodied labor, fantasies, and wounds. The digital photographs in Chen Lingyang’s

lightbox series illuminate an oversize female nude, the artist’s own body, in panoramic Beijing nightscapes (plate 2). She harbors an interior realm of possibility that looms within the “real” world, while also exposing human vulnerability on a monumental scale. In Zhuang Hui’s

, an arresting scene appears amid a dramatically lit, life-size diorama. Artificial grass and flowers sprout from the ground. Against a backdrop of white clouds and blue sky, a thick pink cotton cloud hovers. Framed by a grove of bamboo, a brightly dressed female mannequin stumbles forward with a hand to her face. Her eyes are closed and fake blood drips from them, down her fingers, and onto her orange top. Zhuang created this installation based on a story he read in a tabloid newspaper from southern China, where factories produce transnational consumer goods. Gang members had gouged out the eyes of a female rural migrant factory worker to sell on the black market for human body parts. The technicolor promise of the city produces surreal extremes of stratification and commodification.
zh: 张离《跑、跳、爬、走》中的几件作品探索了迅速变化的社会环境，这种探索被展览场所的历史、其具身劳动、幻想和创伤所放大。陈羚羊《25:00》灯箱系列中的数码照片，以全景式北京夜景照亮一个超大女性裸体——艺术家自己的身体（图版2）。她怀有一个内在的可能性领域，它隐现于“真实”世界之中，同时以纪念碑式的尺度暴露人的脆弱。在庄辉的《六月二十五日，茶山镇》中，一个引人注目的场景出现在戏剧性灯光下、真人大小的立体布景中。人造花草从地面生长出来。在白云和蓝天的背景前，悬着一团浓密的粉色棉云。在一丛竹子的框景中，一个穿着鲜艳的女性人体模型一只手掩面，踉跄向前。她双眼紧闭，假血从眼中滴下，顺着手指流到橙色上衣上。庄辉根据他在南方一份小报上读到的故事创作了这件装置：那里的工厂生产跨国消费品。帮派成员挖出一名农村女工的眼睛，在黑市上出售人体器官。城市色彩斑斓的承诺，制造出超现实的分层与商品化极端。

en: All of these pieces contain holdover socialist sentiments, embedded in the artists’ archival materials, stylistic predispositions, and subject matter, yet were exhibited within the reform-era logic of display in a city where planners and developers strove to command world attention. In contrast with the marketing mission that justified cosred investment in the art center, these artists found in the unfinished, layered aspects of the site a space of imagination. It opened an optical unconscious, inspiring theatrical scenario. Their pieces work through the contradictions embodied in the site’s comingled collectivist and privatized ideologies. Cosmopolitan middle-class lifestyle was built on but also haunted by the displacement of a female urban proletariat and the exploitation of a floating population of rural migrants. This type of site-specific artistic rumination did not align with the vision of Ocean Paradise developers. Their decision to rent out the art center was an interim step toward their next more definitive move.
zh: 所有这些作品都含有残留的社会主义情感，嵌入艺术家的档案材料、风格倾向和题材之中，却是在改革时期的展示逻辑中展出——在一个规划者和开发商力求吸引世界目光的城市里。与为远洋地产投资艺术中心提供理由的营销使命相反，这些艺术家在场地的未完成、多层次特质中发现了一个想象空间。它打开了一种视觉无意识，激发出戏剧性场景。他们的作品处理场地混杂的集体主义与私有化意识形态所体现的矛盾。世界性中产阶级生活方式建立在对女性城市无产阶级的迁置和对农村流动人口剥削的基础上，同时又被它们萦绕。这种场域特定的艺术沉思与远洋天地开发商的愿景并不一致。他们决定把艺术中心出租，是迈向下一步更决定性行动的中途站。

en: Just over two years after the East Modern Art Center was inaugurated with a performance that involved brick throwing, a bulldozer tore into its glass-box renovation of the New Great Factory. Lumbering machines methodically reduced it to the same fate No. 1, No. 2, and No. 3 Cotton Mills had met, and then hauled away the rubble of bricks, concrete, and rebar. In its first phase, the Ocean International Center built on the site included four glassy high-rise towers, the tallest of which rose to thirty-three floors. The towers housed several major Chinese banks, a conference and business center, service apartments, and office space leased by companies such as GlaxoSmithKline, Hewlett-Packard, and Fujitsu. The second phase added two more office buildings connected by a retail mall.

In my interviews with various participants in the East Modern Art Center experiment, I heard different stories. Some told me that if it reaped enough success, it would survive into the future. Others told me that it was always intended to be temporary. It eventually became a kind of installation or performance piece in and of itself.
zh: 远洋艺术中心以一场涉及扔砖的演出开幕两年多后，一台推土机冲进了它对新大厂房的玻璃盒式改造。笨重的机器有条不紊地将其化为国棉一厂、二厂、三厂曾遭遇的同样命运，然后运走砖块、混凝土和钢筋的瓦砾。在其第一阶段，建在原址上的海洋国际中心包括四座玻璃高层塔楼，最高者达三十三层。塔楼容纳数家中国大型银行、会议与商务中心、服务式公寓，以及葛兰素史克、惠普和富士通等公司租用的办公空间。第二阶段又增加两栋由零售商场连接的办公楼。
在采访远洋艺术中心实验的各参与者时，我听到不同的说法。一些人告诉我，如果它取得足够成功，就会延续到未来。另一些人告诉我，它从一开始就打算是临时的。它最终本身成了一件装置或行为作品。

en: The East Modern Art Center preceded new art districts like 798, a Bauhaus-style electronics complex originally built in the 1950s with East German assistance.

When artists and gallerists began renting studio and exhibition space in factories there, it became Beijing’s next center of contemporary art activity, and just as soon was embroiled in debates about art’s commercial cooptation, as well as plans to demolish the factory buildings and develop a high-tech zone. After a protracted struggle between artists and leaders of the landholding company, the area received official designation as the Dashanzi Art District just before the 2008 Olympics.
zh: 远洋艺术中心先于798等新艺术区出现。798是一座包豪斯风格的电子工业建筑群，最初于1950年代在东德援助下建成。
当艺术家和画廊经营者开始在那里租用工作室和展览空间时，它成为北京下一个当代艺术活动中心，并很快卷入关于艺术商业收编的争论，以及拆除厂房、发展高科技园区的计划。经过艺术家与土地持有公司领导层的长期斗争，该地区在2008年奥运会前不久被正式指定为大山子艺术区。

en: likewise marked another trend in the Beijing contemporary art world: in 2001–2, a number of artists produced work focused on rural migrant workers.
Several of these artists described an initial identification with mingong, as they also lived in relatively poor and disenfranchised conditions on the margins of showcase Beijing.

Then as new exhibition and market opportunities arose, they gained new cultural capital and sometimes financial security. Their artistic representation of mingong as emblematic of new forms of social inequality often led to conflicts over ethics or fair compensation. A 2003 group show titled

, curated by Yang Xinyi and featuring the work of fifteen artists, epitomized this phenomenon. Organized in conjunction with a unesco project for rural poverty reduction, the exhibit ran for one week in the newly opened Today Art Museum. The disjuncture between social justice work and contemporary art exhibited in a space like the Today Art Museum emerged in a comment by Huang Ping, a sociologist affiliated with the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and a collaborating member of the unesco project. He bluntly stated, “We are not that happy with the exhibit. We want to show what the migrants contribute to society, but the artists have only depicted their poverty and desperation.”
zh: 《与民工共舞》同样标志着北京当代艺术界的另一趋势：2001至2002年，多位艺术家创作了聚焦农村外来民工的作品。
其中几位艺术家描述了他们最初对民工的认同，因为他们也生活在展示北京边缘相对贫穷、权利被剥夺的条件下。

随着新的展览和市场机会出现，他们获得了新的文化资本，有时也获得经济保障。他们对民工作为社会不平等新形式象征的艺术再现，常常引发关于伦理或公平报酬的冲突。2003年由 Yang Xinyi 策展、十五位艺术家参展的群展《与移民同在》集中体现了这一现象。该展览与联合国教科文组织的一个农村减贫项目合作举办，在新开馆的今日美术馆展出一周。社会正义工作与在今日美术馆这类空间展出的当代艺术之间的脱节，体现在中国社会科学院社会学家、教科文组织项目合作成员黄平的评论中。他直言：“我们对展览不太满意。我们想展示移民对社会的贡献，但艺术家只描绘了他们的贫穷和绝望。”

en: Art as Investment or Public Aesthetics
zh: 作为投资的艺术，还是公共美学

en: The Today Art Museum, conceived as part of the Pingod real estate development on the southern side of the cbd, appeared not long after the East Modern Art Center met its end.

The developers hired the same architect, Yung Ho Chang, to convert a heating plant on the site into a mixed-use sales center and art museum. His studio’s approach to the renovation took into account the structure’s planned obsolesce: “The mix of commercial and cultural activities is strategic although not entirely unique in Beijing. The facility’s temporality means a very quick and low budget job.”
Yet, over a decade later, the museum still stood, and was flourishing.
zh: 今日美术馆是作为中央商务区南侧苹果社区房地产项目的一部分而构思的，在远洋艺术中心终结后不久出现。
开发商聘请同一位建筑师张永和，将场地上的一座供热厂改造成混合用途的售楼处和美术馆。他的工作室对改造的处理考虑了这座建筑按计划将被淘汰的临时性质：“商业与文化活动的混合具有战略性，尽管在北京并非完全独特。设施的临时性意味着工程必须非常快速且预算很低。”
然而十多年后，美术馆依然矗立，并且蓬勃发展。

en: If the East Modern Art Center left itself open to site-specific experimentation or resonance, the Today Art Museum founders cultivated a progrowth culture industry scheme, in which the creation of commodity value for real estate and for contemporary art works were closely intertwined. The design of the museum’s galleries followed the international white cube standard. The museum had a gift center, bookstore, and café, as well as membership and educational outreach programs. It offered storage space to contemporary art collectors. In 2009, it counted Mercedes-Benz, Montblanc, and Shanghai Tang among its many corporate sponsors. In 2010, Credit Suisse underwrote a Today Art Award. Several art magazines were published under the Today imprint, including
(Master) and

(Finance). The former identified and featured the work of “master” artists, often those included in the museum’s collection. The latter provided market analysis, including recent auction statistics for different categories ranging from porcelain to classical ink painting to contemporary art.
zh: 如果说远洋艺术中心为场域特定实验或共鸣敞开大门，今日美术馆的创办者则培育了一种亲增长的文化产业方案，为房地产和当代艺术创造商品价值在其中紧密交织。美术馆展厅的设计遵循国际白色立方标准。馆内设有礼品中心、书店和咖啡馆，还有会员及教育推广项目。它为当代艺术收藏家提供存储空间。2009年，其众多企业赞助商包括梅赛德斯-奔驰、万宝龙和上海滩。2010年，瑞信赞助了“今日艺术奖”。今日品牌旗下出版了几本艺术杂志，包括《大家》和《财经》。前者识别并推介“大师级”艺术家的作品，往往是美术馆收藏中的艺术家。后者提供市场分析，包括从瓷器、古典水墨到当代艺术等不同类别的近期拍卖统计。

en: It might be argued that the success of the Today Art Museum represents the maturing of contemporary art institutions in China. It certainly demonstrates Chinese adoption of the globalizing model of corporate art intervention analyzed in Britain and the United States by Chin-tao Wu.

Under Thatcher and Reagan in the 1980s, public arts funding was increasingly transferred to the corporate sector, which in return was able to raise its public image by trading in cultural respectability. Pingod leaders sent several of the Today Art Museum staff on a research tour of Western museums to study exactly this management model.

The museum they created succeeded in laying claim to a smooth story of bourgeois arrival that contained unruly histories. It did not threaten or invite critique of Beijing as a growth machine in the making.
zh: 或许可以辩称，今日美术馆的成功代表中国当代艺术机构的成熟。它无疑证明中国采纳了吴金桃在英美分析过的企业介入艺术的全球化模式。
在1980年代撒切尔和里根治下，公共艺术资助越来越多地转移到企业部门，企业则借助文化带来的声望来提升自身公众形象。苹果社区的领导者派今日美术馆的几位员工赴西方博物馆考察，专门研究这种管理模式。
他们创建的美术馆成功地把自己包装成一部资产阶级登场的平滑叙事，掩饰了其中桀骜不驯的历史。它既未威胁北京作为一部正在形成的增长机器的运作，也未引发对这一进程的批判。

en: The East Modern Art Center circa 2001 represented a moment in a landscape of museum transformation. It provides a window onto the messy, nascent relationship of state-led urban renewal, privatized real estate, and art. Its embodiment of other ways of being in the city and in the world eventually became part of the wreckage left in the Ocean Paradise wake. Draw into this nexus, artists grappled with how to respond, aesthetically and practically, to the social changes reflected in the art world politics of their everyday lives. They adapted to the new ideological context of cultural industry development in Beijing but not without a struggle over the politics of form. Aesthetics have material consequences because they have the power to promote or puncture particular visions, and artists work at precisely this juncture. The frequency with which Chinese contemporary artists inserted themselves into their own work seems in part a meditation on the question of how their labor and skills fit into this changing landscape.
zh: 2001年前后的远洋艺术中心代表了博物馆转型景观中的一个时刻。它提供了一个窗口，让人看到国家主导的城市更新、私有化房地产与艺术之间混乱而初生的关系。它所体现的在城市与世界中生活的其他方式，最终成为远洋天地身后废墟的一部分。艺术家被卷入这一交织网络，努力思考如何在美学上和实践中回应艺术界日常政治所反映的社会变化。他们适应了北京文化产业发展的新意识形态语境，但并非没有形式的政治斗争。美学具有物质后果，因为它们有能力推动或刺破特定愿景，而艺术家正是工作在这个接合点上。中国当代艺术家频繁把自己插入作品，似乎部分是对其劳动和技能如何融入这一变化景观的沉思。

en: At the Today Art Museum, art was recognized as worth collecting as a financial investment. It contributed to creating a distinct middle-class cultural sensibility for the Pingod real estate development. A 2007 billboard outside of the construction site announced: “cbd • Art Gallery Street • Hotel Lifestyle • Home. Today Art Museum, Asia’s largest Chinese contemporary art gallery, is uniquely linked with the world.” When artists whose engagement with site-specific art once led them out of the studio and into public spaces began to create installations and performances specifically for privatized museum sites like this one, they moved away from a public counteraesthetics.
zh: 在今日美术馆，艺术被认为值得作为金融投资来收藏。它为苹果社区房地产项目塑造独特的中产阶级文化感性作出了贡献。2007年建筑工地外的一块广告牌宣称：“CBD·艺术街区·酒店式生活·家。今日美术馆，亚洲最大的中国当代艺术馆，与世界的独特链接。”当曾因参与场域特定艺术而走出画室、进入公共空间的艺术家，开始专门为这种私有化美术馆场所创作装置和表演时，他们便远离了公共的反美学。

en: In 2007, in the shadow of the partially constructed Koolhaas-designed cctv Headquarters, preparations were underway to demolish the only socialist-era apartment building still standing on the site. Most of the residents had already moved out, but several families refused to leave. With property-based activism on the rise, protest strategies aimed to delay demolition and gain better relocation compensation.

Holdouts became known as “nail households” because they stood out in their resistance to being hammered down into submission. Those in the cctv case had painted graffiti on an exterior wall facing the traffic-congested Third Ring Road. Their slogans, whose aesthetics draw on Chinese traditions of big character posters and socialist murals, included:
zh: 2007年，在部分建成的库哈斯设计央视总部大楼的阴影下，拆除工地上唯一仍存的社会主义时期公寓楼的准备工作正在进行。大多数居民已经搬走，但有几户拒绝离开。随着以财产为基础的行动主义兴起，抗议策略旨在拖延拆迁、争取更好的安置补偿。
拒不搬迁者被称为“钉子户”，因为他们在抵抗被锤打屈服方面格外突出。央视案例中的居民在面向交通拥堵的三环路的院墙上涂写涂鸦。他们的标语在美学上借鉴中国大字报和社会主义壁画传统，包括：

en: The party and its people have suffered disaster.
Is it legal for CCTV officials to steal the people’s property?
Demolition and relocation results from the coalition of government and business.
The Olympics are here, I have no home.
zh: 党和人民遭了灾。
央视领导盗窃人民财产合法吗？
拆迁是官商勾结的结果。
奥运来了，我无家可归。

en: The layers of paint under the large white characters indicated the ongoing battle to speak and to silence. The next day, August 13, 2007, all of the slogans had been painted over in black, including the one declaring: “The darkness of cctv.”
zh: 白色大字下层层叠叠的油漆，表明持续进行的言说与噤声之战。第二天，2007年8月13日，所有标语都被黑色油漆覆盖，包括那条写着“央视的黑暗”的标语。

zh: 图2.07　涂写在“拆”字标记上的“保护”（baohu），央视工地外，2007年。James Tweedie 摄。

en: Adam Chau has analyzed the painting of the big character
(demolish) on the walls of buildings slated for demolition as a text act, a visual form of expression shot through with power.

The formal characteristics of the sign do not just communicate; they act on their audience. This is visual symbolism of a most site-specific nature, as are protests that use the same socialist form of big-character painting against the authoritarian power of urban renewal. On a wall outside the cctv site, blue graffiti painted over a white chai sign spilled outside the circle surrounding the character and declared, “protect!” (figure 2.07). While observers of these emerging forms of activism, which also include protests by laid-off workers seeking more just compensation, see them as a hopeful trend in making growth machine social costs more visible, they also acknowledge that communities often have few resources to rely on in the face of deve-lopment backed by the government.
zh: Adam Chau 将待拆建筑墙上“拆”字的书写分析为一种文本行为、一种渗透着权力的视觉表达形式。

这一标志的形式特征不仅传达信息，还作用于观众。这是最具场域特定性的视觉象征，使用同一社会主义大字报形式的抗议针对城市更新的威权权力，也是如此。在央视工地外的一面墙上，覆盖白色“拆”字的蓝色涂鸦溢出字符周围的圆圈，宣告“保护！”（图2.07）。这些新兴行动主义形式也包括下岗工人争取更公正补偿的抗议。观察者将它们视为让增长机器的社会成本更可见的充满希望的潮流，但他们也承认，面对政府支持的发展，社区往往几乎没有资源可依靠。

en: When artists explored new opportunities for display created by real estate developers, they ran up against limitations to represent in any politically effective way the inherent inequality of showcase Beijing. As Song Dong reflected, “We’re no saviors.” When city residents attempted to resist the imprint of urban development plans on their homes and communities, their protests had little efficacy due to the relative weakness of community power. In terms of China’s booming museum system, this situation translated into few display opportunities independent from progrowth coalition development. Chinese urban planners concerned with the way these coalitions victimize the very people they claim to represent resist the channeling of their labor according to growth machine logic. Their call for planners to recognize the political nature of their work and to “link aesthetic imagination with the public interest” is one that like-minded artists might also heed.
zh: 当艺术家探索房地产开发商所创造的新展示机会时，他们遭遇了限制：无法以任何政治有效的方式再现展示北京内在的不平等。正如宋东所反思的，“我们不是救世主。”当城市居民试图抵抗城市开发计划对其家园和社区的印记时，由于社区权力相对薄弱，他们的抗议收效甚微。就中国蓬勃发展的博物馆体系而言，这种情况意味着独立于亲增长联盟开发项目的展示机会寥寥无几。关心这些联盟如何伤害其声称代表的人们的中国城市规划者，抵制按照增长机器逻辑来引导他们的劳动。他们呼吁规划者认识自身工作的政治性质，“将审美想象与公共利益联系起来”——志同道合的艺术家或许也会听从这一呼吁。

en: How might artists attuned to site-specificity develop a paradigm of community collaboration, on a deeper level than hiring mingong, as part of their practice? Remembering the “failure” of the East Modern Art Center enables historical consciousness about the changing role of museums in China’s capital and how they implicate artists, influence their practice, and frame their artwork. Its history smashed and buried on many levels, what remains is a museum that is neither snow globe nor bell jar, but an archive of alternative possibilities. Scale models of Beijing seductively promise a dreamworld of leisure, culture, and cosmopolitan distinction. They train sight lines in powerful ways, organizing migrant and aesthetic labor alike in their realization. How they meet the ground, however, can also set into motion other arcs of the imagination. The afterimage of a brick hurtling through space shatters their smooth surface into pieces.
zh: 艺术家若要敏锐地对待场域特定性，如何在比雇用民工更深的层面上发展一种社区合作范式，作为其实践的一部分？记住远洋艺术中心的“失败”，可以形成关于博物馆在中国首都角色变化的历史意识，以及它们如何牵连艺术家、影响其实践并框定其作品。它的历史在许多层面上被砸碎、掩埋，所留下的是这样一座博物馆：既不是雪花玻璃球，也不是玻璃钟罩，而是一座另类可能性的档案。北京的比例模型诱惑地许诺一个由休闲、文化和世界性区隔构成的梦想世界。它们以强有力方式训练视线，在实现过程中同样组织着移民劳动与审美劳动。然而，它们如何落地，也可以启动想象力的其他弧线。一块砖头在空中飞驰的残影，将它们的平滑表面击碎成片。

en: These statistics come from the Beijing Cultural Relics Administrative Bureau, which oversees management of museums, and include museums at national, city, district, county, and private levels of administration. National statistics, drawn from China Statistical Yearbooks, for the available ten-year period of 1999–2008 show a 39 percent increase, from a total of 1,364 to 1,893 museums. When the Cultural Relics Administrative Bureau was first founded in 1949, it registered and oversaw only 21 museums around the country. The rapid development of museums as a marker of China’s modernity is reinforced by Shanghai’s hosting of the Twenty-second General Conference of the International Council of Museums in 2010, the same year the city also hosted China’s first World Expo.
